attempt: Try to show a numbered rule defines the native collating sequence, so the unit restates it.
reason: VI.4.4.4 GR6 only USES the term ('the program collating sequence is the native collating sequence'); no rule defines it. GR is right (meaning, IV.3.2).

attempt: State a condition 'next executable statement' has that IV.4.4.2 p5 omits.
reason: The glossary words (next statement to which control will be transferred after the current statement completes) match IV.4.4.2 p5 ('the next COBOL statement to which control is transferred according to the rules above and the rules associated with each language element'); the pointer to IV-25 names that clause.
quoted: The next statement to which control will be transferred

attempt: Scope: glossary limits to Working-Storage and Linkage, perhaps narrower or wider than the rules.
reason: VI.5.2.1 p1 (working storage items with no hierarchical relationship are noncontiguous elementary items) and X.4.1.1 p1 (same for Linkage) cover exactly the two sections the glossary names.
quoted: which bear no hierarchic relationship to other data items

attempt: The glossary adds the full-character-set content of a nonnumeric literal.
reason: IV.4.2.2.2.1 p1 gives the quotation-mark delimiting and IV.4.1 p1 says 'In the case of nonnumeric literals ... the character set is expanded to include the computer's entire character set'; nothing is left over.
quoted: may include any character in the computer's character set

attempt: Glossary restricts content to digits plus optional sign, a possible extra obligation.
reason: VI.5.9.4 GR3b: 'its content ... must be one or more numeric characters; if signed, the item may also contain a +, -, or other representation of an operational sign' states both halves.
quoted: if signed, the item may also contain

attempt: The glossary requires one or more numeric characters, sign leftmost, point not rightmost.
reason: IV.4.2.2.2.2 p1 (characters from digits, signs, point; 1-18 digits), SR2 (sign leftmost) and SR3 (point not rightmost) state each sentence.
quoted: The decimal point must not be the rightmost character

attempt: Glossary says OBJECT-COMPUTER is an Environment Division paragraph; a rule might not say so.
reason: VI.4.4.1 p1 'provides a means of describing the computer on which the program is to be executed' and IV.6.2.2 p2 (Configuration Section has the SOURCE-COMPUTER, OBJECT-COMPUTER and SPECIAL-NAMES paragraphs) give the same.
quoted: name of an Environment Division paragraph

attempt: The term 'entry' with clauses describing the environment might be new.
reason: VI.4.4.2 format shows the entry's clauses (MEMORY SIZE, PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE), IV.6.2.3.1 names object-computer-entry, VI.4.4.1 p1 states the describing purpose. Weakest of the set but the same content.
quoted: which contains clauses which describe the computer environment

attempt: Try to show a rule states the object program definition or the 'program' alone convention.
reason: No rule in the standard defines 'object program' or the convention; a definition of meaning, GR.
quoted: the word 'program' alone may be used

attempt: Try to show a rule defines 'obsolete element'.
reason: Clauses apply the term (e.g. VI.4.4.1 p1) and the module table explains the Z letter, but no rule defines it; GR definitional stands.
quoted: is to be deleted from the next revision

attempt: Glossary says the phrase of OPEN picks the mode and the state ends at CLOSE without REEL/UNIT.
reason: OPEN GR1 (VII.4.3.4) 'results in the file being in an open mode', CLOSE GR7 'the file is removed from the open mode', plus OPEN GR4/GR5 and Table 2 columns Input/Output/I-O/Extend map phrases to modes.
quoted: before the execution of a CLOSE statement without the REEL or UNIT phrase

attempt: 'positive or negative' might add a meaning beyond 'algebraic properties'.
reason: IV.4.3.5 p1 defines operational signs as associated with signed numeric items and literals 'to indicate their algebraic properties'; the sign of a value is its positive or negative property, so no further obligation.
quoted: to indicate whether its value is positive or negative

attempt: The second sentence says the object program interrogates for presence of an optional file.
reason: OPEN GR1 'determines the availability of the file', Table 1 optional-file row and GR13 (sets the file position indicator for an optional input file not present) state the interrogation and its result; FILE-CONTROL GR2 states the declaration.
quoted: declared as being not necessarily present

attempt: Glossary says optional words are reserved words only for readability.
reason: IV.4.2.2.1.3.2 p1: 'uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format' is the same.
quoted: only to improve the readability of the language

attempt: Glossary gives a timing for entering the output procedure.
reason: SORT GR11 'control passes to it after the file ... has been sequenced' and MERGE GR9 'Before entering the output procedure, the merge procedure reaches a point at which it can select the next record in merged order' match both clauses.
quoted: after the sort function is completed

attempt: Glossary says a padding character fills unused positions in a physical record.
reason: PADDING CHARACTER GR1 'any portion of a block which exists beyond the last logical record will be filled entirely with padding characters'; SR1/SR3 state the character kinds; block is the physical record.
quoted: used to fill the unused character positions

attempt: Try to show PAGE/LINAGE rules define 'page'.
reason: LINAGE GR2 defines page body and the PAGE clause defines lines per page, not the term; no rule states 'a vertical division of a report'. GR stands.
quoted: A vertical division of a report

attempt: Glossary page body might differ from LINAGE's.
reason: LINAGE GR2 'That part of the logical page in which these lines can be written and/or spaced is called the page body.' is identical.
quoted: lines can be written and/or spaced

attempt: Glossary adds 'end of the page' placement.
reason: TYPE GR7 'specifies a report group that is processed by the report writer control system as the last report group on each page' covers the placement.
quoted: presented at the end of a report page

attempt: Glossary adds 'beginning of the page' placement.
reason: TYPE GR3 'first report group on each page' covers the placement.
quoted: presented at the beginning of a report page

attempt: State what the unit defines that IV.6.1.2 p1, IV.7.3.3 p1 and the format do not: a paragraph header is a reserved word followed by the separator period, indicating the beginning of a paragraph, in the Identification and Environment Divisions.
reason: The reader's quoted IV.6.1.2 p1 says only that headers 'identify the type of information contained in the paragraph'; IV.7.3.3 p1 says a paragraph is a header plus entries but not that the header is a reserved word plus a separator period. Only format notation implies it. Doubt: back to a reader as a row candidate (SR, definitional).
quoted: A reserved word, followed by the separator period

attempt: The list might permit headers the format omits (or the reverse).

quoted: PROGRAM-ID. AUTHOR. INSTALLATION. DATE-WRITTEN.

attempt: The unit might state something beyond introducing the Environment list, such as that only these headers are permitted.
reason: It is a single clause ending in a colon with no definition of its own; the list unit p216 completes the sentence and carries the words.

attempt: The list might permit headers the format omits.
reason: IV.6.2.3.1 shows SOURCE-COMPUTER, OBJECT-COMPUTER, SPECIAL-NAMES, FILE-CONTROL, I-O-CONTROL, the same five.
quoted: SOURCE-COMPUTER. OBJECT-COMPUTER. SPECIAL-NAMES. FILE-CONTROL.

attempt: Glossary adds that a paragraph-name is a user-defined word that begins a paragraph.
reason: IV.4.2.2.1.1 item 11 lists paragraph-name as a user-defined word, IV.4.2.2.1.1.3 p1 'names a paragraph in the Procedure Division', IV.6.4.1.2 p3 'A paragraph consists of a paragraph-name followed by a period and a space'.
quoted: identifies and begins a paragraph
